verdict: Both are about the same. Calories and protein are the same, and the difference in fat is very small.
why: Both are an estimated 650 kcal per bowl.
Protein is also the same, an estimated 22 g each.
Curry laksa has an estimated 36 g fat, curry mee 34 g. Both come from the santan (coconut milk) broth.
What makes the biggest difference is how much broth you finish, not which noodle you choose.
when_a: Curry mee is okay for an occasional lunch. Add chicken or egg for protein.
when_b: Curry laksa is okay when you're craving it. Enjoy one bowl and balance it with lighter food at other meals.
tip: Eat the noodles, chicken and vegetables first. Leave half the santan broth in the bowl to save calories.

faq.q: Is the tauhu pok (tofu puffs) in curry high in calories?
faq.a: Tauhu pok soaks up the santan broth, so it adds calories. Just have a few pieces, no need to avoid it completely.

faq.q: Is there a lighter option if I'm craving curry?
faq.a: Try Penang laksa or mee soto as an alternative. If you still want curry, drink less of the broth and choose plain water.
